workout.tip.basis: Each step decides for itself whether it uses power, heart rate or pace: click a step's target to change it (marked "Set"). Steps marked "Auto" follow the session type (easy road runs / long runs use power, with heart rate capped at your easy-run ceiling; trail runs use heart rate; intervals use power). The numbers come from your current CP, LTHR, easy-run ceiling and threshold pace.
workout.tip.chart: The horizontal axis is time ("until lap button" steps are drawn at a fixed width, hatched); height and color both show intensity (≈ % CP). Heart-rate steps are converted to a power height as an estimate, which only affects this chart. Click a step to select it below.
workout.tip.tss: TSS (est.) = Σ seconds × IF² × 100 ÷ 3600, IF = target midpoint ÷ CP; heart-rate steps map Friel HR zones to Palladino power zones, and steps with no target get a fixed value by type. All estimates; how far running rTSS differs from this formula is unverified.
workout.tip.rules: Live checks: zone 5 reps at least 2 min each (a Taiwanese coach); zone 5 rests no longer than the shortest rep and no more than 3 min (Buchheit); zone 3 reps at least 3 min each (Haugen 2022, lower bound); the day's time cap (schedule preferences: a soft cap only warns, a hard cap blocks); errors such as choosing power without a CP. Quality sessions are also compared with this level's standard workout to see whether they count as a step up.
workout.tip.lastRest: No rest after the last rep: go straight into the next step. COROS interval groups can't do this, so the push flattens it into individual steps (one lap each).
workout.tip.watch: COROS watch limits: running power only takes absolute watts (no % CP); one target per step; no ramp steps. Below are the steps that will actually be sent.
workout.tip.tpl: Workouts with a source (author / book / URL under each one), filtered by this session's type. Quality sessions come in three families, judged first by main-set intensity, then by rep length: Aerobic intervals (≤ 101% CP; long tempo 15–30 min per rep, cruise intervals 6–15 min, shorter ones count as cruise too), VO2max intervals (above threshold, 2–5 min per rep, rest about 1:1; short-on/short-off like 30/30 also go here) and Speed (≤ 2 min per rep, rest ≥ 2×, e.g. R, strides, short hill sprints). Trail runs come in three: structured climbing (stairs, steady-grade routes; HR / power ranges set as usual), technical terrain (time + climb + RPE, no HR or power target; RPE ≥ 7 counts as a quality session) and downhill technique / eccentric (time + descent). Each one has a line on its training purpose. Each step uses its source's own target: Palladino / Stryd use power; Friel, Uphill Athlete and Pfitzinger use heart rate; Daniels, Canova and Billat use pace (converted only when the app lacks the source's number, marked as an estimate). Once inserted they are ordinary steps you can edit; an edited quality session is judged as a step up or not by its own reps and intensity. At the top of each family are this session's three "recommended" picks (for quality sessions, #1 = the next step on the interval ladder); the rest are folded below.
workout.tip.total: Total time is the sum of the steps below: to change the time, change the steps (clicking here opens the structure).
workout.tip.pacePct: Pace % is a multiple of your threshold pace: bigger = slower (e.g. 114–129% is Friel zone 2).
workout.tip.rpe: RPE on a 0–10 scale (Foster): 3 moderate, 5 hard, 7 very hard, 10 maximal. On technical terrain and downhills heart rate stays low and power is unreliable, so only RPE and climb / descent count; the watch gets no target for this step, and the RPE and climb go in the step name. A max of 7 or higher makes this a quality session (48 h from other quality sessions). Load is counted from what the watch records.

workout.load_rpe_tip: By feel: Easy / Somewhat hard / Hard / Very hard / Max are Borg CR-10 2 / 4 / 5 / 7 / 10; TSS = {factor} × RPE × minutes (Foster session RPE, {src}, estimate). Planning targets only: the actual load is the watch's record.

workout.load_rpe_default: default factor, no activity with a watch-recorded RPE yet
feas.how_text: "Time to get ready?": your last 4 weeks, a little more each week with an easy week every 4th, up to 3 weeks before the race. "Ready now?": the longest outing and the biggest week you actually did in the last 6 weeks. Both are compared with the race's hardest day. Advice only, your event is never changed; the thresholds are estimates.
